claim_scores.rationale: It reproduces the init failure with `track_best_outputs=True`, catches `AssertionError`, and asserts the message mentions `track_stats`.
The accepted run uses `valset=trainset` and enables both `track_stats=True` and `track_best_outputs=True` during `GEPA(...).compile(...)`.
It monkeypatches `gepa.optimize` before `compile`, so the import inside `GEPA.compile` resolves to `fake_optimize` and runs against a controlled result while compiling with `track_best_outputs=True`.
The successful configuration accesses `optimized.detailed_results`, showing the compiled program gains that attribute when `track_stats` is enabled.
`fake_optimize` returns `best_outputs_valset`, and the compiled program exposes the same data at `optimized.detailed_results.best_outputs_valset`, demonstrating passthrough from the optimizer result.
It checks concrete contents, asserting validation-task index `0` and a `Prediction` list whose first item has `answer == "A"`.
